The *Cūḷadhanuggahajātaka* (Ja 374) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka. According to the traditional framework preserved in the commentary, the Buddha related this story while residing at Jetavana concerning a monk who had fallen under the temptation of his former wife. When the monk admitted that longing for his former wife made him regret taking monastic ordination, the Buddha remarked that this woman had also harmed him in a previous life by causing his head to be severed, subsequently relating the past life tale at the assembly's request.
